markdown_report:
**Prioritize a scoring-path audit before changing GRU4Rec’s memory mechanism.** At 10% progress, resolving failed execution checks remains the clearest next experiment; additional architectural proposals lack supporting temporal measurements.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) All four categories fail final-feature consistency, with discrepancies of 0.000163–0.000633; their cause remains unresolved. (2) Reported valid-feature and candidate-score errors are zero despite final-feature differences. Confirm that these comparisons actually executed on aligned, nonempty tensors before interpreting zeros. (3) Positive sampled training margins and unavailable temporal metrics establish neither recent-context utility nor validation improvement.

**Insights from related work.** (1) GRU recurrence can update states on zero inputs [1]; padding invariance requires skipped padding transitions. (2) Batched and individual computations can differ numerically [2], motivating repeated configurations and float64 references without treating either as ground truth. (3) Metamorphic testing motivates equivalent-execution tracing [3]; elementwise comparisons and explicit coverage prevent skipped checks from appearing successful [5].

**Framework and directions.** Retain three linked directions: execution equivalence, scoring-path dependence, and behavioral sensitivity. Controls are identical-history batch transformations, analytical feature interventions, and final-item-fixed history perturbations; outputs are tensor discrepancies, score/margin changes, and paired ranking changes. Behavioral interpretation follows relevant execution verification.

| Atomic idea | Originality | Potential | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Execution-to-score trace [1–3,5–6] | 4: focused integration; established testing | 7: resolves blocking ambiguity; indirect accuracy benefit | 4: bounded replay; export instrumentation requires care |
| Final-item-fixed shuffle [1–2] | 4: isolates earlier order; familiar perturbation | 7: guides memory experiments; in-sample distribution shift limits inference | 3: existing hooks; paired uncertainty needs care |
| Hidden-state restoration [4] | 6: transfers patching to recommendation GRUs; established intervention | 7: separates attenuation from readout sensitivity; donor choice matters | 6: frozen model; recurrent replay requires instrumentation |

**Selected algorithm: execution-to-score trace.** Freeze category fixtures, mappings, architecture, checkpoint hashes, histories and ordered candidates. Strictly load identical parameters/buffers into ModelView and exported implementations. Compare repeated, singleton, duplicated, permuted and partitioned executions, restoring row order; include mixed lengths, maximum lengths, repeats and empty histories.

Trace cloned embeddings, recurrent outputs/hidden states, maximum-nonzero-position features, projections and raw scores. Hold padding, initial states, precision and backend settings fixed. Record each check as pass, fail, skipped or error, with reasons, compared-element counts and nullable errors. Preserve prespecified atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4; apply elementwise reference-relative checks. Report coverage, violations, top-10 changes and boundary margins separately. Investigate numerical differences through repeated executions and float64 references; never relax tolerances to unlock results.

For a verified affine scorer, write s=Ah+b. Compare measured score changes with Aδ; use zero interventions and observable directions. For competitor j, δ=±εg/‖g‖, where g=A_t−A_j, predicts margin change ±ε‖g‖. Handle zero g explicitly. Distinguish raw-score dependence, centered-score dependence and actual ranking changes; unchanged ranks do not imply an unused feature path. Optional SVD nullspace controls require residual checks and may be unavailable.

Preserve diagnostic APIs, existing metrics, model modes, RNG states and runtime accounting. Keep one GRU4Rec checkpoint/category and every benchmark constraint fixed. Proven semantic corrections require consistent retraining and predictor-writer updates; official macro validation HR@10 alone selects models. These computational interventions establish neither user intent nor generalization.

idea.description: Trace identical histories through GRU4Rec execution, final-state selection and exported candidate scoring, using explicit comparison coverage and analytical feature interventions to resolve observed final-feature discrepancies before interpreting temporal effects.
idea.motivation: All four execution checks fail while reported candidate-score discrepancies are zero. Those zeros could reflect executed agreement, incomplete coverage, insensitive score directions or a reporting problem. The evidence supports resolving this ambiguity before changing recurrent memory; strong training margins alone cannot establish useful temporal dependence.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve embedding and sampled-margin probes and actual view.model access through compatible item_emb, log2feats(sequence), and predict_score(features, items). Loader batches remain (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors.

Freeze a bounded fixture suite for each of the four categories: raw histories, truncated left-padded tensors, ordered candidate IDs, ID mappings, architecture configuration and checkpoint SHA-256. Save fixtures and results beneath the trial directory. Include singleton, mixed-length, maximum-length, repeated-item and explicitly handled empty histories. Generate candidates from public training histories without hidden evaluation files; preserve their identities and order throughout comparisons. Document fixture-selection rules and counts. This is an execution audit, not an alternative benchmark.

Strictly load the same category checkpoint into training-side and exported implementations; compare parameters and buffers exactly. Exercise the actual emitted predictor's preprocessing, routing and score path. If intermediate hooks or an exported scoring entry point are inaccessible, report that coverage as skipped with a reason rather than replacing it with a surrogate. Use eval() and inference_mode(), matching device, dtype, initial hidden states, batch shape, autocast and TF32 settings. Record software/hardware versions and deterministic settings. Save and restore model modes, Python/NumPy/Torch RNG states, CUDA RNG states and any backend settings changed during the audit. Snapshot hook outputs recursively with detach().clone() so later operations cannot overwrite captured values.

Repeat identical singleton and batched executions separately, then compare singleton, duplicated, permuted and partitioned batches against a designated reference after restoring row identities. Hold weights, histories, padding and reset initial states fixed. Validate shapes and finiteness first. Trace embeddings, recurrent outputs/hidden states, final readouts, output projections and raw candidate scores where accessible. Gather the maximum nonzero sequence index, never count-1; empty rows have no valid readout index and follow the trained empty-history behavior, including any score bias. Compare per-position B x L x K scores with a small loop reference, explicitly broadcasting candidate dimensions.

Represent every check with status executed/pass, executed/fail, skipped or error; include reason, reference identity, compared-element count, dtype, error location, violation count and nullable error statistics. Zero error requires an executed nonempty comparison. Report coverage separately from pass rates. Preserve the previous audit's atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4 for continuity, documenting that they are prespecified audit thresholds rather than universal numerical guarantees. Require every element to satisfy abs(actual-reference) <= atol + rtol*abs(reference). Report maximum absolute error and relative errors using a documented denominator, but never substitute a global relative statistic for elementwise checks. Any exploratory tolerance analysis remains separate and cannot retroactively change primary results.

Separate identical-input transformations from changed-padding comparisons. An unpadded history is an equivalent reference only if the trained recurrence skips padding transitions. Do not silently replace the supplied corrected backbone. If packing is actually used, verify that nonpadding events are compacted chronologically into right-padded temporary tensors before packing, positive lengths are on CPU, enforce_sorted=False is used and outputs are restored to original positions. Empty rows must bypass packing. Directly packing left-padded tensors discards valid suffix events. For a unidirectional packed GRU, compare its last-layer final hidden state with the aligned final valid output. If the implementation processes leading padding, report that semantic fact; changed-padding outputs cannot automatically be classified as numerical failures.

Where supported, compare singleton and batched paths with float64 computations using identical weights and inputs converted before execution. Reduced discrepancies support a numerical explanation but do not prove correctness. Unsupported float64/backend comparisons are skipped with reasons. Float64 is a diagnostic reference, not exact ground truth or a deployment change. Persistent indexing, row-order or predictor disagreements require semantic investigation. Report raw score changes, centered score changes, supplied-candidate order, exact ties, top-10 IDs/overlap and score margins around rank 10. Use the pinned evaluator's tie rule when available; otherwise report exact-tie ambiguity and avoid claiming evaluator parity.

For feature-to-score dependence, first establish the actual scoring equation. If s(h)=Ah+b, with A=EW for the implemented projection convention, compare measured score(h+delta)-score(h) against A delta while fixing weights, biases and candidates. Biases cancel only from score differences. Include a zero intervention. For a nonzero target-competitor gradient g=A[target]-A[competitor], use delta=±epsilon*g/||g||; predicted margin change is ±epsilon*||g||. Freeze competitor selection and epsilon before examining results, for example the highest-scoring nontarget candidate and epsilon=0.01*max(||h||,1e-8). Report g=0 as feature-insensitivity for that pair, not a global scoring failure. For a nonzero scoring positive control, a nonzero row of A supplies an observable direction; an SVD right singular vector is an optional alternative. Do not apply affine formulas across an intervening nonlinear normalization or nonlinear scorer: intervene after that operation or use the actual equation with an explicitly scoped numerical check.

Distinguish computational dependence from ranking dependence: common score shifts preserve all margins, and small margin changes need not change rank. An optional synthetic boundary-crossing check can derive a displacement from an observed margin, but must recompute every competitor and be labeled a constructed computational test, not a recommendation-quality result. Optional matched-norm SVD controls distinguish ker(W), ker(A), and ker(CA), where C centers candidate scores. Verify residuals, document singular-value thresholds and report trivial nullspaces or nonexistent nonzero common-shift controls. These controls are supplementary and must not turn a bounded audit into an expensive search.

Unresolved checks leave affected temporal metrics null with reasons; retain unaffected descriptive metrics. Once relevant checks pass, run the already prespecified paired temporal probe without tuning perturbations to favorable outcomes. Label training-prefix effects as conditional in-sample sensitivity. Preserve separate full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for twenty real training users, five/category. Use no unavailable ratings, review text, item categories, prices, stores, inferred compatibility or simulator traits.

Preserve all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch and single-GPU execution. Each category loads exactly one independently trained GRU4Rec checkpoint: no additional fitted predictor, fusion or checkpoint averaging. A proven correction that changes model semantics requires consistent retraining and updates to the embedded predictor writer and loader; never repair only diagnostic execution and attribute it to the original checkpoint. Do not read other trials or hidden test files. Record diagnostic runtime against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Official host macro validation HR@10 alone selects models. Fixed fixtures can miss other execution failures, and training-prefix diagnostics can reflect memorization; neither audit success nor analytical score dependence demonstrates generalization or removes validation-search selection bias.
idea.pseudocode:
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    save model modes, RNG states and backend settings
    try:
        set actual model to eval; enter inference_mode
        retain existing embedding and sampled-margin measurements
        fixtures = load_or_create_prespecified_trial_local_fixtures()
        record checkpoint hash, mappings, architecture and environment
        strictly load same checkpoint into available exported implementation
        compare parameters and buffers exactly
        for configuration in [singleton, batched]:
            repeat identical execution with reset hidden states
            snapshot accessible intermediate tensors with detach().clone()
            record within-configuration variation
        reference = replay_fixed_reference_configuration(fixtures)
        for execution in [singleton, duplicate, permute, partition]:
            replay identical histories, padding, weights and initial states
            restore original row identities
            trace embeddings, recurrence, final readout, projection and scores
            validate shapes and finiteness
            compare each element with abs(a-r) <= 1e-5 + 1e-4*abs(r)
            record status, coverage, counts, violations and nullable errors
        separately audit empty rows and actual padding semantics
        where supported, repeat equivalent paths in float64 as diagnostic references
        for fixed nonempty fixture:
            h = feature at maximum nonzero sequence position
            establish actual scorer equation and intervention location
            test zero displacement
            if scorer is affine at that location:
                select prespecified competitor and displacement scale
                compare measured score changes with A @ delta
                compare measured margin changes with analytical predictions
                report zero-gradient cases explicitly
                optionally verify feasible matched-norm nullspace controls
            else:
                use scoped checks of the actual nonlinear score equation
            distinguish raw scores, centered scores, margins, ranks and top-10
        compare ModelView and actual exported predictor in supplied candidate order
        if relevant checks remain failed, skipped or unresolved:
            mark affected temporal metrics null with explicit reasons
        else:
            run the existing prespecified paired temporal probe
        retain separate simulator-user full-catalog recommendations
        record synchronized diagnostic runtime
    finally:
        restore model modes, RNG states and backend settings
    return {metrics, metric_definitions}

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    include measured metrics, definitions, comparison coverage and unresolved checks
    distinguish executed zero errors from skipped or missing measurements
    request evidence-linked findings and alternative explanations
    separate numerical variation, semantic defects and behavioral sensitivity
    distinguish computational score dependence from ranking or recommendation utility
    prohibit inferred intent and unmeasured validation improvement

originality.positive: Combines execution coverage, exported-predictor parity and analytical feature-to-score controls around a concrete GRU4Rec inconsistency.
originality.negative: Metamorphic testing, tensor tracing, affine perturbation identities and nullspace controls are established methods; novelty lies in their integration.

future_potential.positive: Can resolve a blocking ambiguity and provide reusable evidence for subsequent recurrent-memory experiments.
future_potential.negative: Its impact is primarily diagnostic; passing fixed fixtures neither improves ranking directly nor establishes generalization.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses bounded inference and existing checkpoints without fitting additional predictors; advanced SVD controls remain optional.
code_difficulty.negative: Strict export parity, intermediate instrumentation, comparison coverage, precision references and state restoration require more implementation care than the previous score of 3 suggested.

related_work.title: [1] PyTorch GRU and packing documentation
contributions: Specifies recurrent equations showing why zero inputs need not leave hidden states unchanged.

Defines recurrent outputs and final hidden states; companion packing documentation explains prefix-based packing: https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence.html.
limitations: Does not establish whether the supplied trained implementation skips padding transitions.
Packing left-padded inputs directly does not preserve valid suffix events; chronological compaction is required.

related_work.title: [2] PyTorch numerical accuracy notes
contributions: Explains why batched and individual floating-point computations can differ.
Supports separating execution configuration and precision effects when investigating discrepancies.
limitations: Does not establish that observed discrepancies are harmless or justify a universal tolerance.
Float64 comparisons are diagnostic references rather than exact ground truth.

related_work.title: [3] Model-level metamorphic testing
contributions: The supplied search summary motivates testing equivalent model executions for inconsistencies.
limitations: Does not provide measured findings for this GRU4Rec checkpoint or benchmark.
The proposed tracing and feature interventions are task-specific adaptations.

related_work.title: [4] Heimersheim and Nanda: activation patching guidance
contributions: Motivates complementary restoration and disruption interventions and careful metric selection.
limitations: A GRU4Rec adaptation requires recurrent replay and suitable controls.
Patching effects do not establish user intent or validation gains.

related_work.title: [5] PyTorch testing documentation
contributions: Documents elementwise absolute and reference-relative tolerance comparisons.
Supports explicit shape, dtype and numerical comparison checks.
limitations: Passing numerical comparisons cannot establish semantic correctness without valid reference executions and sufficient coverage.

related_work.title: [6] PyTorch reproducibility and deterministic algorithms
contributions: Documents randomness control and reproducibility limitations across execution environments.
Companion deterministic-algorithm documentation describes enforcement and unsupported operations: https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.use_deterministic_algorithms.html.
limitations: Repeatability does not imply correctness or guarantee agreement across devices and releases.
Deterministic settings can change performance or reject unsupported operations and must be recorded and restored.
